correctness.rationale: The Fourier decomposition is complete: Q² one-dimensional irreps and q-1 central Schrödinger irreps of degree Q account for qQ² regular dimension. Subgroup averages become rank-one projections onto the constant vector and delta_0, with overlap Q^(-1/2), producing eigenvalues (1±Q^(-1/2))/2 and the claimed multiplicities. Plancherel yields the exact positive-time chi-square formula; fair X/Y label words of at most two runs have probability t/2^(t-1), while three-run XYX and YXY convolutions are within (1-1/q)/Q of Haar. These imply two-sided TV bounds and the q^(m+1)4^(-t) chi-square scale, respecting t>=1 and fixed m. Independently reconstructed full integer-group convolution for (q,m)=(2,1),(3,1),(5,1), t=1..4, and checked rational chi-square and TV inequalities. These finite cases do not prove all prime powers; the representation and run arguments do.
residual_risks: An arbitrary uniform-Lagrangian walk is not this two-fixed-subgroup measure; finite checks do not establish general characteristic-four formulas.
